# Skill: bk7258-worktree-build

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

## Acceptance boundary

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

`tab magic code error 0xffffffff` 也确实没有阻止后续校准和 Wi‑Fi 初始化，与权威固件的行为一致；本次无需处理。

`trace isr drain: samples=32` 后紧跟 `trace read wake: ... samples=0` 不是“ISR 没保存 ADC 数据”。ISR 的顺序是：

```text
填充 s_adc_buf 至 32
→ rtos_set_semaphore()
→ bk_adc_stop()
→ bk_adc_stop() 将 sample_cnt 重置为 0
→ 等待线程醒来
```

缓冲区内容没有因 `sample_cnt` 清零而被擦除，随后仍被 `bk_adc_read_raw()` 拷贝。因此 `samples=0` 只是这个调试点在 stop 之后观测到的状态，不能当作 ADC 采样失败。

这里的 `WRONG_PASSWORD` 是上层 WPA 对“2/4 没成功送达 AP”的通用归因，**不能据此认定密码错误**。更底层的事实是：

对比两份日志，失败原因已经很清楚：**不是 PSK/MIC 计算、不是 ADC、不是 RF 初始化卡死；是 OpenVela 发出的 EAPOL M2（4-way 的第 2 帧）在 802.11 MAC 层没有获得 AP ACK，而且 MAC 没有进行重传。**

权威 Armino 的成功路径很短：

```text
16884  收到 AP 的 M1（len=113）
16885  STA 发送 M2（len=135）
16890  收到 AP 的 M3（len=169）
16891  STA 发送 M4（len=113）
16894  add CCMP
```

也就是 M2 发出后约 5 ms，AP 已回 M3；说明 M2 成功到达 AP，PSK/MIC 通过校验，握手继续。

当前 OpenVela 的路径则是：

```text
State: ASSOCIATED -> 4WAY_HANDSHAKE
RX message 1 of 4              # M1 收到
Sending EAPOL-Key 2/4          # M2 已生成并提交 TX

txcfm ... eth=8e88 ... ack=0 done=1 tid=7
l2tx cfm ... acked=0 ... retry=0 swretry=0
__l2_packet_send: send failed
```

这个序列重复三次，然后 WPA 才报告：

```text
4-Way Handshake failed - pre-shared key may be incorrect
WRONG_KEY / WRONG_PASSWORD
```

这个“密码可能错误”是上层 WPA 的泛化结论，不是证据。因为：

- 若密码/MIC错误，M2 仍会先在空口获得 AP 的 802.11 ACK（`ack=1`），之后 AP 不发送 M3或发送断开；
- 当前是 M2 在更低层就得到 `ack=0`；
- 且每次 `retry=0`、`swretry=0`，它甚至没有正常的 MAC 重传机会；
- 因此 AP 很可能根本没有成功收到 M2，尚未走到验证密码/MIC 的阶段。

当前与 Armino 的关键差异：

| 阶段 | Armino | OpenVela |
|---|---|---|
| Association | 成功 | 成功 |
| 收到 EAPOL M1 | 成功 | 成功 |
| 生成并提交 EAPOL M2 | 成功 | 成功 |
| 空口 ACK | 可由后续 M3 证明成功 | 明确 `ack=0` |
| MAC 重传 | 成功路径无需显式观察 | `retry=0`, `swretry=0` |
| 收到 EAPOL M3 | 有，约 5 ms 后 | 没有 |
| 完成 CCMP | 有 | 没有 |

本次 SARADC 修复是有效的：日志已经完整跑过

```text
temp_code=31,...
cali bias(e)
cali bias(f)
calibration_main(...) over
wifi runtime init success
```

并且后续温度补偿持续有效，例如 `adc_code=507 / 486 / 477 / 494`。因此 ADC 不再是这次握手失败的直接原因。

当前根因应收敛为：

```text
EAPOL M2
→ TID 7 / AC_VO
→ OpenVela 的 TX descriptor / TX-confirm / retry 配置或状态机
→ done=1 but ack=0 and retry=0
→ WPA 将发送失败误映射成 WRONG_PASSWORD
```

最值得检查的不是 WPA 密码处理，而是 `rwnx_start_xmit` 到 TX-confirm 之间、专门承载 EAPOL 的 QoS/Voice 队列路径：描述符 flags、retry policy、sta/vif/chan context、TX confirm 状态解析，以及为何 `retry=0`。

那帮我在 OpenVela 驱动里找一下 txcfm/l2tx 这段代码，看看 ack 和 retry 是怎么解析的
并且对比armino的代码，如有差异，则和adc这部分一样，彻底抄过来
我会在 `bk7258-wifi-rebuild` 中从 `txcfm → l2tx cfm → rwnx_start_xmit/descriptor` 完整追到状态位解析，再逐文件比对 Armino 的实际编译源码。若确认存在移植差异，我会仅迁入该差异对应的 authority 逻辑、保留现有无关改动，并完成构建/包解码验证。

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

```bash

readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text

<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before

processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text

cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

结论：我已把 `txcfm → l2tx cfm → EAPOL 回调` 与 Armino 逐段对过，**没有发现 OpenVela 把 `ack` 或 `retry` 解析错的活跃代码差异，因此没有做“整段抄回”的无效修改。**

关键事实：

- 两边 `TX_STATUS_*` ABI 完全一致：

```c
DONE              = bit 0
RETRY_REQUIRED    = bit 1
SW_RETRY_REQUIRED = bit 2
ACKNOWLEDGED      = bit 3
```

因此日志中的：

```text
status=00001
ack=0 done=1 retry=0 swretry=0
```

在 Armino 和 OpenVela 中含义相同：MAC 确认该帧处理结束，但没有收到 802.11 ACK，也没有要求 host 重投或软重投。

- 两边的确认消费函数相同：
  - `fhost_tx_cfm_push()` 读取 `txdesc->host.cfm.status`；
  - 若 bit 1/2 被置位，走重投；
  - 若 bit 3 被置位，通知成功；
  - 仅 bit 0 时，走失败回调，WPA 的 M2 发送返回失败。

  OpenVela 的对应位置在 [rwnx_tx.c](/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/third_party/beken_armino/glue/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:1209)。

- M2 的实际提交路径也与权威一致：

```text
rw_task:bmsg_tx_handler
→ rwnx_start_xmit
→ fhost_txbuf_push / closed MAC
→ closed MAC 回填 txdesc->host.cfm.status
→ fhost_tx_cfm_push
→ rwnx_tx_confirm
→ l2_packet TX callback
→ WPA 认为 M2 发送失败
```

  EAPOL 会走 [rw_task.c](/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/third_party/beken_armino/glue/bk_wifi/src/rw_task.c:178) 的 `rwnx_start_xmit()` 分支，非旧 `rw_msdu` 路径。

- OpenVela 与 Armino 使用的 BK7258 闭源库也完全一致：

| 库 | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `libwifi.a` | `6e7e018c884674ced3305d241138eae004c4c3d8568123573c24ec9c71d37b0c` |
| `libbk_phy.a` | `fb3e8f6a6782f6fab6edde59ec95417c0da1da2ab8263230848535b34e4a6979` |

也就是说，`status=0x1` 不是 OpenVela 的 TX-confirm 解码器凭空制造的；是同一个闭源 MAC/PHY 运行在当前 OpenVela 环境中，实际写回的状态。

有两个配置差异，但都不是当前 M2 未 ACK 的直接修复点：

- 权威启用 `CONFIG_MAC_SFRAME_SOFTWARE_RETRY=y`，当前未启用；但权威 [rwnx_tx.c](/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:183) 自己把对应的 EAPOL 软件重投实现硬编码在 `#if 0` 中，因此仅打开配置不会使 M2 自动重传。
- 权威启用 `CONFIG_RWNX_QOS_MSDU=y`，当前未定义；其控制的是旧 `rw_msdu.c` 发送路径，而日志已证明 EAPOL M2 走 `rw_task → rwnx_start_xmit`，且描述符观测过 `tid=7`、`queue=3 (AC_VO)`、有效 STA/VIF，故不能把它作为 M2 的直接解释。

OpenVela 的 [rwnx_tx.c](/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/third_party/beken_armino/glue/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c) 相对权威的活跃差异是诊断输出，例如 `txcfm`、`l2tx cfm` 和 `txq miss` 探针；它们不修改 `cfm->status`、描述符 flags、ACK 判断或重投分支。直接还原整文件只会删掉定位证据，无法把 `0x1` 改成 `0x9`。

因此当前最准确的根因边界是：

```text
同一份闭源 libwifi/libbk_phy
+ OpenVela 的 SoC/RTOS/IRQ/时钟电源/内存运行环境
→ M2 提交至 MAC
→ MAC 实际回填 DONE=1、ACK=0、无 retry 请求
→ WPA 失败
```

下一步应查**闭源库进入硬件前后的平台契约**，而不是再改 `txcfm/l2tx`：

1. TX 完成中断来源、ICU 映射和确认回调时序；
2. MAC/PHY 时钟、复位、power vote 与 DVFS 状态；
3. TX descriptor 的 DMA 可见性、cache/内存属性和 status write-back 地址；
4. AP 已关联后的 STA/信道上下文和 MAC 重试控制寄存器。

这部分存在真正的 OpenVela 平台实现差异，且比 `rwnx_tx.c` 的 ACK 位解析更接近 `ack=0, retry=0` 的来源。

    50	static int bk7258_wifi_isr_trampoline(int irq, void *context, void *arg)
    51	{
    52	  struct bk7258_wifi_isr_slot *slot = arg;
    53	  (void)irq;
    54	  (void)context;
    55	  if (slot != NULL && slot->callback != NULL)
    56	    {
    57	      unsigned idx = (unsigned)(slot - g_wifi_isr);
    58	
    59	      bk7258_wifi_isr_count[idx]++;
    60	      if (idx == INT_SRC_SARADC)

    62	          syslog(LOG_INFO, "[SARADC-PORT] source=8 ISR count=%lu\n",
    63	                 (unsigned long)bk7258_wifi_isr_count[idx]);
    64	        }
    65	      slot->callback(slot->arg);
    66	    }
    67	  return OK;
    68	}

    70	bk_err_t bk_int_isr_register(icu_int_src_t src, int_group_isr_t callback,
    71	                             void *arg)

    73	  int ret;
    74	
    75	  if (src >= 64 || callback == NULL)

    78	    }
    79	
    80	  if (g_wifi_isr[src].callback != NULL)

    82	      bk7258_icu_disable(src);
    83	      irq_detach(16 + src);
    84	    }
    85	
    86	  g_wifi_isr[src].callback = callback;
    87	  g_wifi_isr[src].arg = arg;
    88	  ret = bk7258_icu_attach(src, bk7258_wifi_isr_trampoline,
    89	                          &g_wifi_isr[src]);
    90	  if (ret < 0)

    93	      g_wifi_isr[src].arg = NULL;
    94	      return BK_FAIL;
    95	    }
    96	
    97	  return bk7258_icu_enable(src) == OK ? BK_OK : BK_FAIL;

Background sub-session "Trace authority TX-completion interrupt chain" (actor_id: explore-2) completed.
Result: ## BK7258 iperf authority TX-completion chain

**Scope/result:** the complete LMAC/MAC portion is present only in the pinned opaque archive, not C source. The authority build map identifies the exact object members and symbols; open source provides the SoC IRQ wrappers, task scheduling, and `fhost_tx_cfm_push` tail.

1. **MAC completion IRQ → generic CPU IRQ dispatch**
   - The TX-completion-bearing MAC source is expected on **`INT_SRC_MAC_TXRX_MISC` → CPU IRQ 32** (MAC TX/RX misc); this is the TX-confirmation path used by the opaque Wi-Fi core.
   - Mapping: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/soc/icu_map.h:62`
     ```c
     {INT_SRC_MAC_TXRX_MISC, 32, IQR_PRI_DEFAULT, GROUP1}
     ```
   - Source enum: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/include/driver/int_types.h:46-51`.
   - CPU0 ICU gate is `cpu0_wifi_mac_int_tx_rx_misc_en`, bit 0 of the high interrupt-enable bank:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/soc/sys_reg.h:983-984`;
     helper enable is in `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/soc/bk7258/hal/sys_hal.c:1720-1722`.
   - Vector wrapper: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/bk7258/interrupt.c:258-261`:
     `MAC_INT_TX_RX_MISC_Handler()` calls `ARCH_ISR_HANDLER(32)`.
   - `ARCH_ISR_HANDLER` gets the registered callback with `arch_interrupt_get_handler(irq)` and invokes it, with optional trace/stat accounting:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/driver/bk7258/interrupt.c:52-78`.

   Other enabled MAC sources are relevant to the whole LMAC engine but are not independently proven as the ordinary data-TXC source by available source: TX/RX timer=31, RX trigger=33, TX trigger=34, protocol trigger=35, general=36, HSU=37, wakeup=38 (`icu_map.h:61-68`). The actual MAC-status decode and source-specific ISR registrations live in the opaque `libwifi.a`.

2. **Opaque LMAC event production and confirmation-list enqueue**
   - Authoritative build: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/build/bk7258/iperf/bk7258/app.map`.
   - Exact opaque ownership:
     - `txl_cfm_push` — `libwifi.a(txl_cfm.c.obj)`, map lines **27496-27498**, address `0x020c341c`.
     - `txl_cfm_evt` — same object, **27504-27506**, address `0x020c3518`.
     - `txl_cfm_init` — **27513-27515**.
     - `txl_cfm_evt_bit` — **27520-27522**.
     - `macif_tx_cfm_start/push/done` — `libwifi.a(macif_fhost.c.obj)`, **31510-31519**, addresses `0x08011e74/78/c8`.
   - The generated contract declares per-queue event bits:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/include/generated/lmac_msg.h:243-249,322-327`.
     `KE_EVT_TXCFM_AC0..AC3` always exist; `KE_EVT_TXCFM_BCN` is gated by `NX_BEACONING`. `KE_EVT_TXCFM_MASK` combines them at `:349-361`.
   - `rw_tx_buffering.h:72-76` explicitly documents the ordering model: TX descriptors are retained on the CFM queue and freed only when the **TX_CFM kernel event** is handled. Thus the hardware ISR/event producer does not directly free the descriptor or run the host callback.

3. **Event/task handoff**
   - Wi-Fi initialization invokes opaque `rwnxl_init()` before RF calibration:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/wifi_init.c:80-105`.
     This is where the opaque Wi-Fi core initializes its MAC/LMAC/CFM state and registers the MAC handlers.
   - `rwnx_intf_init()` subsequently starts the `core_thread` event handler and `kmsgbk` message thread (`wifi_init.c:101-105`).
   - The kmsg worker blocks on `app_sema`, receives messages, then executes `ke_evt_none_core_scheduler()`:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rw_task.c:105-121`.
   - The core worker processes a bus message, releases any waiting message semaphore, then invokes `ke_evt_core_scheduler()`:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rw_task.c:910-917` and `:1013-1019`.
   - Both scheduler implementations are opaque `libwifi.a(ke_event.c.obj)`: map **25676-25681**. They consume `KE_EVT_TXCFM_*`, call opaque `txl_cfm_evt`, and bridge via opaque `macif_fhost.c.obj`.

   **Practical serialized order:** IRQ/MAC status → opaque handler fills `txdesc->host.cfm`, queues descriptor through `txl_cfm_push`, sets the queue event bit → core scheduler selects TXCFM event → `txl_cfm_evt` drains it → `macif_tx_cfm_*` invokes the externally linked `fhost_tx_cfm_push`. There is no source-level direct caller of `fhost_tx_cfm_push` because that call is inside `libwifi.a(macif_fhost.c.obj)`, while the callee is linked from `libbk_wifi.a(rwnx_tx.c.obj)`.

4. **FHOST confirmation / application callback**
   - Declaration: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/include/rwnx_tx.h:39`.
   - Implementation: `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:965-1103`.
   - `cfm->status` must contain `TX_STATUS_DONE` (`lmac_tx.h:7-16,107-131`). Otherwise it logs an invalid confirmation and does nothing (`rwnx_tx.c:1100-1101`).
   - Under the active software-TXQ configuration:
     - `TX_STATUS_RETRY_REQUIRED`: clear status; restore queue credit; reject absent/inactive queue; preserve retry sequence for newer ABI; requeue and invoke `rwnx_hwq_process()` (`rwnx_tx.c:987-1022`).
     - `TX_STATUS_SW_RETRY_REQUIRED`: same integrity checks, increment `sw_retry_cnt`, cap at `CFG_MAX_SW_RETRY_CNT`, then requeue (`:1037-1076`).
     - `TX_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGED`: terminal success calls `rwnx_tx_confirm()` (`:1091-1094`).
     - all other done statuses: terminal failure calls `rwnx_tx_confirm()` (`:1095-1099`).
   - Terminal callback/free path is `rwnx_tx_confirm()`:
     `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:154-215`.
     It returns flow-control credits, starts/stops the queue according to `credits`, calls `skb->cb(skb->args, acknowledged)`, then `kfree_skb(skb)`.
   - This creates the required ordering: **retry/requeue first; only terminal completion calls the user callback and frees ownership.**

## Gates and ordering/timing primitives

- Active iperf authority config:
  - `CONFIG_WIFI_ENABLE=1`, `CONFIG_RWNX_SW_TXQ=1`,
  - core task priority/stack `2/2048`,
  - kmsg task priority/stack `3/4096`,
  from `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/build/bk7258/iperf/bk7258/config/sdkconfig.h:74-95`.
- `NX_VERSION` is **v6.8.2.0**:
  `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/include/rwnx_version.h:31-50`.
  Therefore the `NX_VERSION >= 6.22` `hostid` branches are not active in this authority build; the SW-TXQ code uses the older `host.buf` ABI branch.
- Event inclusion gates:
  - `NX_BEACONING`: BCN confirmation bit/mask;
  - `NX_TX_FRAME`: internal TX-frame confirmation;
  - `BK_MAC` + `NX_SW_TXQ`: SW TXQ event;
  - see `lmac_msg.h:226-275,302-360`.
- Retry lifetime primitive: management retries are permitted only while
  `!time_after(bk_get_tick(), skb->jiffies + RWNX_MGMT_TXQ_MAX_QUEUE_JIFFIES)`;
  `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:142-152`.
- Queue ordering and liveness guards:
  - CFM queue/event handoff prevents freeing during ISR context;
  - `txq->idx == TXQ_INACTIVE` prevents resurrecting a flushed/disconnected queue;
  - `cfm->status = 0` occurs before requeue;
  - `txq->credits` is restored before `rwnx_txq_start()` / hardware processing.
- Bus-message handling explicitly uses `GLOBAL_INT_DISABLE()` in its critical portions (`rw_task.c:125-130`), while CFM finalization is serialized by the event scheduler/core worker rather than being executed from the MAC vector.

## Comparison: `bk7258-wifi-rebuild`

Concrete differences only:

1. **Same opaque LMAC boundary remains.**  
   `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/prebuilts/libwifi.a` still owns `txl_cfm_*`, `ke_evt_*`, `macif_tx_cfm_*`, and MAC status decode. The imported C `fhost_tx_cfm_push` is only the downstream callee, so it cannot independently repair a missing MAC-completion interrupt/event handoff.

2. **The terminal CFM state machine is authority-equivalent except diagnostics.**  
   Target:
   `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/third_party/beken_armino/glue/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:1209-...`.
   It adds the `final_cfm_seq` / `RWNX_LOGW("txcfm ...")` probe at **1218-1251** before the authority retry/terminal branches. The authority starts its equivalent logic at `/home/czp/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/components/bk_wifi/src/rwnx_tx.c:973`. The added probe changes observability, not ownership/retry ordering.

3. **ICU source IDs and per-source gates match, but routing is NuttX-owned.**  
   Target’s `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/glue/include/driver/int_types.h:73` retains `INT_SRC_MAC_TXRX_MISC = 32`; target HAL enables the matching CPU0 TX/RX-misc and TX-trigger bits in:
   `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/hal_port/hal_port_sys_int_power.c:82,92`.
   Unlike authority, it has no copied `interrupt.c` vector wrapper or `icu_map.h`; it delegates registration/routing to the team NuttX chip layer through:
   `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/glue/hw_driver_shim.c:122-126`.
   Therefore, a target failure where IRQ 32 never increments is **upstream of `txl_cfm_evt`**, not a defect in `fhost_tx_cfm_push`.

4. **Configuration alignment is intentional.**  
   Target glue has `CONFIG_RWNX_SW_TXQ=1`, core `2/2048`, kmsg `3/4096` in:
   `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/glue/include/common/sys_config.h:134-140`,
   matching authority’s active branch and scheduling dimensions.

5. **Target has explicit completion diagnostics unavailable in authority source.**  
   `/home/czp/openvela_contest/.worktrees/bk7258-wifi-rebuild/chips/bk7258/wifi/bk7258_wifi_lower.c:922-928` records per-source interrupt counts specifically to distinguish “completion interrupt never arrives” (enable/routing failure) from later event/CFM handling failure. This is the correct probe boundary for this chain.

对比结论：TX-completion 的 ICU 映射目前没有发现与 Armino 不一致、足以造成 `ack=0` 的错误；也不能把 source 29/30 当作 TX 完成中断。

正确的 BK7258 映射是：

| ICU source | 含义 | 权威 CPU IRQ |
|---:|---|---:|
| 29 | MODEM / PHY MPB | 29 |
| 30 | MODEM_RC / PHY RIU | 30 |
| 31 | MAC TX/RX timer | 31 |
| 32 | MAC TX/RX misc，TX-confirm 候选来源 | 32 |
| 33 | MAC RX trigger | 33 |
| 34 | MAC TX trigger | 34 |
| 35 | MAC protocol trigger | 35 |
| 36 | MAC general | 36 |

权威侧的 source 32 向量明确是：

```c
MAC_INT_TX_RX_MISC_Handler()
{
    ARCH_ISR_HANDLER(32);
}
```

OpenVela 当前也是：

```text
source 32
→ NVIC_IRQ_FIRST + 32
→ NuttX IRQ handler
→ Wi-Fi callback trampoline
```

而 source 32 的 CPU0 高位中断使能位也对齐权威：

```c
cpu0_wifi_mac_int_tx_rx_misc_en
```

OpenVela 的 `hp_bk_wifi_interrupt_init()` 已按权威顺序启用：

```text
MAC general
→ MAC protocol trigger
→ MAC TX trigger
→ MAC RX trigger
→ MAC TX/RX misc
→ MAC TX/RX timer
→ MODEM
```

其中 `MAC TX/RX misc` 在 OpenVela 和权威都写入 CPU0 高位 bank 的 bit 0。

更重要的是，当前板端日志已经出现：

```text
txcfm ... st=00001 ack=0 done=1
l2tx cfm ... acked=0 done=1 retry=0 swretry=0
```

这意味着 TX completion 不只是“可能到达”：它已经走完了以下链条，进入了 OpenVela 的 `fhost_tx_cfm_push()`：

```text
MAC completion event
→ 闭源 libwifi.a: txl_cfm_push / txl_cfm_evt
→ 闭源 libwifi.a: macif_tx_cfm_*
→ OpenVela: fhost_tx_cfm_push()
→ rwnx_tx_confirm()
→ EAPOL 回调报告发送失败
```

因此，当前证据排除两种说法：

- 不是 TX-completion IRQ 完全没来；
- 不是 OpenVela 把 `TX_STATUS_ACKNOWLEDGED` 位解析错了。

两边状态位 ABI 相同：

```text
0x1 = DONE
0x2 = RETRY_REQUIRED
0x4 = SW_RETRY_REQUIRED
0x8 = ACKNOWLEDGED
```

所以 `0x1` 的含义没有歧义：闭源 MAC 最终确实回填了“发送处理完成、但未 ACK、且未请求 host 重试”。

还有一个实现层面的差异，但它目前不是已证实根因：

- Armino 的 ICU 驱动内部维护 group0/group1 的 ISR 表；
- OpenVela 直接把 source 映射到 NuttX 的 NVIC IRQ。

不过 BK7258 的权威向量同样是逐 source 的：source 32 就进 IRQ 32。因此这不是“应该聚合到一个 IRQ、当前却错误分开”的证据。权威 `group_isr()` 是其驱动内的注册/状态管理层，而不是 source 32 必须改接别的 CPU 向量的证明。

下一步最有价值的是让板端在一次 M2 失败后打印 source 29–36 的计数。当前代码已经有这个诊断输出：

```text
[BK7258-WIFI] isr 29=... 30=... 31=... 32=...
[BK7258-WIFI] isr 33=... 34=... 35=... 36=...
```

判据是：

- source 32 在 M2 前后增长：MAC completion IRQ 和 NuttX 路由可达；问题更靠近闭源 MAC 对该帧的空口/重试判定、或 CFM 事件的内容。
- source 32 不增长、但 `txcfm` 仍到达：TXC 可能不是 source 32，需从闭源库的实际 MAC 状态路径继续识别。
- source 32 不增长且没有 `txcfm`：才应回头检查 source 32 的 NVIC/ICU 绑定。
- source 32 增长但 M2 仍固定 `0x1`：中断映射不是直接根因，应转查 MAC 的 TX retry policy、MAC/PHY 时钟/功率状态、描述符 DMA 可见性和空口发送参数。

本轮没有修改代码或烧录。
你排查一下
我会继续把问题收敛到可验证的中断/事件边界：先确认 `0903` 日志实际运行的是哪一版镜像、source 31–36 是否已注册并计数、以及 `txcfm` 出现前后是否能证明 IRQ 32 或闭源 event scheduler 的执行。不会先改代码。

thinking: We need distinguish whether TX completion is missing, delayed, or correctly delivered with an unacknowledged result. The decisive observation is that `txcfm` and `l2tx cfm` appear with `status=0x1`: the opaque MAC completed the descriptor and the opaque confirmation/event path reached the host callback. Therefore an ICU route failure that prevents completion delivery is incompatible with the observed log. We then compare source IDs, gates, registration, and authority vector mapping. Source 32 is a candidate TX/RX-misc source, but the opaque library registers 29, 30, 31, 33, 34, 35, and 36; it does not register 32 through the OSI callback. The source-32 CPU gate is still enabled, matching Armino. Existing per-source counters are emitted only from the NuttX scan-result-export path, which the direct `bk7258_wifi_runtime connect` flow does not necessarily traverse, so their absence from the log cannot be interpreted as zero interrupts.

text:
排查结论：当前没有证据表明 TX 完成中断的 ICU 映射、回调时序或 `txcfm` 解析导致了 `ack=0`。

已经确认的链条是：

```text
EAPOL M2 提交
→ 闭源 libwifi MAC/LMAC 完成该 TX descriptor
→ 写入 txdesc->host.cfm.status = 0x1
→ txl_cfm_push / txl_cfm_evt
→ macif_tx_cfm_*
→ OpenVela fhost_tx_cfm_push()
→ rwnx_tx_confirm()
→ WPA 收到发送失败
```

最关键的板端证据仍然是：

```text
txcfm ... st=00001 ack=0 done=1
l2tx cfm ... acked=0 done=1 retry=0 swretry=0
```

这说明完成事件不是没到、也不是在 NuttX IRQ 路由中丢失。`fhost_tx_cfm_push()` 只有在 `TX_STATUS_DONE` 已置位后才会走到日志位置；而它看到的是闭源 MAC 已写好的 `0x1`。

ICU 映射与权威的对比结果：

| Source | 作用 | 权威 IRQ | OpenVela IRQ |
|---:|---|---:|---:|
| 29 | MODEM / PHY MPB | 29 | 45 (`16 + 29`) |
| 30 | MODEM_RC / PHY RIU | 30 | 46 |
| 31 | MAC TX/RX timer | 31 | 47 |
| 32 | MAC TX/RX misc | 32 | 48 |
| 33 | MAC RX trigger | 33 | 49 |
| 34 | MAC TX trigger | 34 | 50 |
| 35 | MAC protocol trigger | 35 | 51 |
| 36 | MAC general | 36 | 52 |

权威的 source 32 向量也是单独的：

```c
MAC_INT_TX_RX_MISC_Handler()
{
    ARCH_ISR_HANDLER(32);
}
```

OpenVela 的 `source → NVIC_IRQ_FIRST + source` 对 BK7258 source 32 是同一个编号模型，并非错误地把 source 32 接到了另一向量。

同时，CPU0 中断使能也对齐：

```text
authority:
cpu0_wifi_mac_int_tx_rx_misc_en = high-bank bit 0

OpenVela:
hp_sys_hal_enable_mac_txrx_misc_int()
→ cpu0_wifi_mac_int_tx_rx_misc_en(1)
```

还有一个容易误会的点：

- `0903-vela-5.log` 中看不到 source 31–36 的 attach 日志，不能推导“它们没有注册”。
- 其他同类板端日志已有明确证据：source `36/35/34/33/31` 分别 attach 到 IRQ `52/51/50/49/47` 并成功 enable。
- source 32 没有通过 `_bk_int_isr_register` 注册，这是当前闭源库的实际行为；但它的 gate 仍按权威开启。
- source 29/30 是 PHY MODEM 中断，**不是 SARADC，也不是 TX completion 本身**。SARADC 是 source 8。

当前代码虽然有每 source 计数器：

```text
[BK7258-WIFI] isr 29=... 30=... 31=... 32=...
[BK7258-WIFI] isr 33=... 34=... 35=... 36=...
```

但它只在 NuttX Wi‑Fi lower 的“扫描结果导出”回调中打印。你跑的是 `bk7258_wifi_runtime connect` 的 vendor runtime 路径，该路径不保证经过这个 NuttX lower 扫描导出点，因此 `0903` 没有这两行不能视为“计数为零”。

所以当前中断层面的结论是：

```text
ICU/完成事件链：已足以把 CFM 送到 host
CFM 状态内容：闭源 MAC 真实回填 DONE=1、ACK=0
问题不在 host 对 ACK 位的解释，也不在“TX complete IRQ 消失”
```

下一步不应该再改 `txcfm/l2tx` 或盲目调整 ICU source。最有效的是在 `fhost_tx_cfm_push()` 的确认点旁边做一次定向关联日志：记录 M2 前后的 source `31/33/34/35/36` 增量、`cfm->status`、queue、TID、STA ID。这样能直接回答：

- source 34/36 是否确实伴随 M2 completion 增长；
- CFM 是否是普通 MAC completion，而非超时/flush 合成；
- 该 descriptor 在 MAC 内得到 `0x1` 前的 TX 事件是否正常。

但即使这些 IRQ 计数都正常，根因仍将收敛在更靠近空口/MAC 的层面：该描述符为何被 MAC 作为“已完成但未 ACK、无 retry 请求”处理。
好，那就在 fhost_tx_cfm_push 加关联日志，打印 M2 前后 source 31/33/34/35/36 的计数增量和 status、queue、TID、STA ID

我会在 `fhost_tx_cfm_push()` 加一个仅针对 EAPOL M2（`ethertype=0x888e`）的定向关联探针：快照每个描述符提交时的 source `31/33/34/35/36` 计数，并在该描述符 CFM 到达时打印增量、`status`、queue、TID 和 STA ID。这样不依赖扫描回调，也避免对普通流量刷屏。先核对当前 TX 文件的未提交改动和 descriptor 生命周期，再做单文件合并修改。

# Skill: bk7258-worktree-build

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

## Acceptance boundary

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.

你说得对：我此前只看了前 74 行，结论不完整。`/tmp/0907-vela-3.log` 是一个追加了至少两次启动/测试的完整日志；关键证据在后半段。

结论先说：

1. 文件前半的 ADC 初始化失败，确实存在，但它不是这份文件后半 EAPOL 失败的当前状态。
2. 文件后半已证明 SARADC、RF 校准、Wi‑Fi 初始化全部跑通。
3. EAPOL M2 失败时，MAC `GENERAL` 中断 source 36 在提交到 CFM 期间稳定增长；因此不是“TX 完成 IRQ 根本没来”或 host 的 CFM/event 链完全断掉。
4. 闭源 MAC 最终持续回填 `status=0x1`：`DONE=1, ACK=0, retry=0, swretry=0`。问题仍在 MAC 对 M2 的实际空口 ACK/retry 判定，或其更早的 PHY/MAC 状态，而不在 `txcfm/l2tx` 的位解析。

## 这份文件有两段完全不同的运行

### 第一段：旧的初始化失败

第 24–73 行：

```text
[wifi] wifi initing
[cal] load polar ...
[adc] trace acquire enter
[adc] trace acquire lock=0
...
[bk7258_wifi_runtime] connect: init did not complete
```

这里确实没有进入 `trace read wait`、ADC ISR、`temp_code`、`cali bias`。

而 `init did not complete` 不是 `bk_wifi_init()` 的即时错误返回；应用层是启动初始化线程后，轮询 `bk7258_wifi_is_ready()` 最多 300 次、每次 100 ms，也就是等约 30 秒后才打印这个消息。因此它只证明：这一轮启动在 30 秒内没有就绪。

这与当时错误启用 `CONFIG_SARADC_NEED_FLUSH` 的症状一致：在 HAL 绑定硬件指针前错误走进 `adc_flush()`，无法继续进入 ADC 上电和校准。

### 第二段：后续重启后的完整成功初始化

从第 75 行的新 NSH 会话、约第 94 行再次执行连接开始，路径完全不同：

```text
[wifi] wifi initing
[cal] get rfcali_mode:1
[adc] trace acquire lock=0
[adc] trace read wait ...
[adc] trace isr complete
[adc] release
[cal] temp_code=31,dmodldosel=4,Dgmdc=7
[cal] cali bias(e)
...
[cal] cali bias(f)
[cal] calibration_main(e1c2bcd) over
[cal] rf cali flag in flash: valid
flash txpwr table:0xf
```

这是 SARADC 修复生效的强证据：

- ADC 中断实际发生；
- 每轮采满 32 个样本；
- 等待线程被唤醒；
- `release` 已执行；
- 温度码正常返回；
- 两阶段 `cali bias` 完成；
- `calibration_main()` 完成。

之后也确实进入了关联和 4-way，而不仅是“初始化看起来完成”：

```text
State: ASSOCIATED -> 4WAY_HANDSHAKE
WPA: RX message 1 of 4-Way Handshake
WPA: Sending EAPOL-Key 2/4
```

所以此时 ADC、温补、RF 初始化不再是当前 M2 失败的直接阻塞点。

## 这份日志其实已经包含新的 EAPOL IRQ 关联探针

我前面说“需要刷入关联探针”是不准确的；这份完整日志已经有它。每个 EAPOL CFM 都是：

```text
eapol cfm st=00001 q=3 tid=7 sta=0 d31=0 d33=0 d34=0 d35=0 d36=3
eapol cfm st=00001 q=3 tid=7 sta=0 d31=0 d33=0 d34=0 d35=0 d36=3
eapol cfm st=00001 q=3 tid=7 sta=0 d31=0 d33=0 d34=0 d35=0 d36=5
```

后续关联重试也重复相同模式，只是 STA ID 在 `0`、`1` 之间变化：

```text
st=00001 q=3 tid=7 sta=1 d31=0 d33=0 d34=0 d35=0 d36=3
```

这组数据的严格含义是：

| 字段 | 观察值 | 结论 |
|---|---:|---|
| `st` | `0x00001` | 闭源 MAC 写回 `TX_STATUS_DONE`，未写 ACK 或 retry 位 |
| `q` | `3` | EAPOL 走 AC_VO，符合预期 |
| `tid` | `7` | EAPOL 被正确分类为最高用户优先级 |
| `sta` | `0` / `1` | AP station entry 已存在，不是 `INVALID_STA_IDX` |
| `d31` | `0` | 该描述符期间未观测到 MAC TX/RX timer source |
| `d33` | `0` | 未观测到 RX trigger source |
| `d34` | `0` | 未观测到 TX trigger source |
| `d35` | `0` | 未观测到 protocol trigger source |
| `d36` | `3` 或 `5/6` | EAPOL 入队至 CFM 期间，MAC general source 持续触发 |

这非常重要：EAPOL M2 的确认不是“中断没来”。在每个 M2 入队后，MAC general IRQ 都触发了数次，并最终抵达：

```text
txcfm ... st=00001 ack=0 done=1
l2tx cfm ... acked=0 done=1 retry=0 swretry=0
```

因此可排除：

```text
M2 提交后完全没有 MAC IRQ
→ 不成立

MAC completion event 没进入 txl_cfm / fhost_tx_cfm_push
→ 不成立

OpenVela 把 ACK bit 错读成 0
→ 不成立
```

需要保留一个边界：探针按你的要求记录 `31/33/34/35/36`，**没有记录 source 32**。因此不能从 `d31/d33/d34/d35=0` 推导 “source 32 一定没有触发”。但 source 36 已经稳定增加，且 CFM 已到 host，当前无法把问题归结为 IRQ 路由断裂。

## 真正失败点

每次都是：

```text
WPA: RX message 1 of 4-Way Handshake
WPA: Sending EAPOL-Key 2/4

eapol cfm st=00001 q=3 tid=7 sta=...
txcfm ... ack=0 done=1
l2tx cfm ... acked=0 done=1 retry=0 swretry=0

__l2_packet_send: send failed
```

这说明：

```text
M1 已收到
M2 已正确生成
M2 已正确归类为 TID 7 / AC_VO
M2 已提交给 MAC
MAC general IRQ / CFM event 已运行
但闭源 MAC 最终判定 M2 未获 ACK，且没有请求重传
```

之后 WPA 才把这个底层 TX 失败归类成：

```text
WRONG_PASSWORD
```

这不是密码错误的证据。若密码或 MIC 错误，通常 M2 依然应先获得 802.11 ACK；之后 AP 不返回 M3、或在更高层拒绝。这里是更早的 MAC CFM 已确报告 `ACK=0`。

## 日志尾部还有一个次级现象

在运行时命令 30 秒结束、已经回到 NSH 后，自动重连仍继续，随后出现：

```text
rw_msg_send timeout for 7169
lmac_connect_cfm ret=-6144 status=47
...
Authentication ... timed out
```

这不是最初五次 4-way M2 失败的根因；它发生在应用命令已经报告超时之后，属于自动重连与高强度 verbose UART 输出仍在运行时出现的后续关联超时。应在下一轮干净启动、只执行一次连接时单独观察，避免把这个后续重连状态和 M2 的 `ACK=0` 混为一因。

当前最准确的状态是：

```text
SARADC / 温补 / RF 校准：已恢复，完成
ICU / MAC general 事件 / CFM 调度：可达
EAPOL descriptor / TID / queue / STA ID：正确
CFM status：闭源 MAC 稳定回填 DONE=1, ACK=0, retry=0
```

下一步应继续从闭源 MAC 为什么对这个已关联、已正确分类的单播 M2 不置 `ACKNOWLEDGED` 入手：空口 TX 速率/保护参数、MAC retry policy、或关联后 MAC/PHY 状态，而不是再回头改 ADC、`txcfm` 解析或 ICU 路由。
那就把 M2 的 TX 速率和保护参数打出来，看看发的什么 rate、是否没跟 AP 协商对

# Skill: bk7258-worktree-build

# BK7258 Worktree Build

## Complete workflow

Prefer the bundled end-to-end wrapper. Without `--flash` it performs the safe
build, L1 validation, package, independent decode, and package-integrity gate:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --jobs 12
```

The wrapper derives one stable slot per worktree under
`cmake_out/bk7258-worktrees/`. Its `build/cp` and optional `build/ap` directories
are reused for normal Vela incremental builds, and its `package` directory is
safely replaced on each successful package run. A binding file ties the slot to
the canonical workspace/worktree paths, so another worktree cannot reuse it.
If a component defconfig changes, only that component's generated build cache
is recreated. Use `--fresh` to deliberately recreate this worktree's generated
build cache. Use `--slot NAME` only to choose a stable human-readable slot.

To flash, rerun in an interactive terminal and explicitly add `--flash`:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

To flash an existing verified package without rebuilding or requiring a
workspace/worktree, give the image and the board tools directory explicitly:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/full_flow.sh \
  --image /absolute/path/to/all-app.bin \
  --tools-dir /absolute/path/to/board/bk7258-devkit/tools \
  --flash --device /dev/ttyUSB0
```

Image-only mode requires `manifest.json` and `decode-report.json` next to the
image. It runs the same independent integrity gate and automatic flash wrapper
but skips build/package. `--worktree <feature-worktree>` may replace
`--tools-dir`; the wrapper then derives `board/bk7258-devkit/tools` from that
worktree.

Flashing is destructive and must use an interactive terminal. The PTY wrapper
streams the loader output without buffering and drives the reset itself: once
the loader prints `connect success`, the wrapper opens the same serial device
as a second writer and injects `reboot bootloader` into the running NSH
console. Target firmware carrying the bootloader-reset patch
(`feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset`, `board_reset`
`ENTER_BOOTLOADER` via AON WDT) then performs a chip-level reset with the
vendor warm-jump tag cleared and the reset reason recorded as watchdog, so
the BootROM runs the cold chain and BL2 opens the download listen window
that the already-polling loader catches by itself -- no manual reset.
`Gotten Bus...` produces the handshake-success banner. If the automatic
reset does not engage within a few seconds (firmware without the patch, a
hung console), the wrapper retries once and then falls back to bell-and-
prompt manual resets, numbered 1, 2, ...; press reset on each prompt and
stop after the success banner. Never press reset after `Begin EraseFlash`,
and never type into the terminal during the automatic phase.

The public workflow assumes a trusted, current-user-owned workspace and Git
worktree. It does not defend against malicious processes running as the same
Unix user, SIGKILL, power loss, or tools that ignore its mapping lock. It never
runs worktree scripts through `sudo` and refuses to
run as root. Give the normal user access to the serial device through the
platform's serial-device group (commonly `dialout`). Before writing, the
wrapper verifies the audited `bk_loader` SHA-256, prints the complete image
SHA-256. The explicit `--flash` flag is the authorization switch. The agent
must still announce the target device and complete image hash in commentary
immediately before launching it.

When an agent launches the flash stage for the user, it must first announce in
commentary the target device, the complete image SHA-256, and that the wrapper
injects `reboot bootloader` automatically (manual-reset fallback prompts
appear only if the auto reset does not engage), then run the command with
interactive terminal support. Never launch `--flash` in the background,
through redirected output, or in a non-interactive shell. Keep the turn open
until `Writing Flash OK` or a clear failure is reported.

The existing board scripts remain the authority: `bk7258-package.sh` must
produce `decode pass`, and `bk7258-flash.sh` must reproduce the report, validate
all hashes, save the loader log, and find `Writing Flash OK`.

## Scope

This workflow is for a BK7258 team-repository worktree whose sources are
linked into the parent OpenVela workspace. The parent workspace is the
directory containing both `build.sh` and `nuttx/`; it is not the team-repository
checkout and not the worktree directory itself.

Never build a BK7258 worktree by passing `board/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp` to
`build.sh`. That path is valid for repository-local Python tools, but
`build.sh`/`lunch` resolves board configs through the manifest path under
`vendor/beken/boards/...`.

## 1. Establish the worktree mapping

For normal worktree builds, use the bundled wrapper; it serializes access to
the shared mapping and restores both links on exit:

```bash
<skill-dir>/scripts/build_worktree.sh \
  --workspace <openvela-workspace> \
  --worktree <feature-worktree> \
  --component cp \
  --jobs 12
```

Use `--component ap` for AP. Use `--output /absolute/output/path` only for an
isolated build whose artifacts will be passed explicitly to packaging.

From the parent OpenVela workspace, verify the mapped paths:

```bash
readlink -f vendor/beken/chips/bk7258
readlink -f vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit
```

For a feature worktree, both targets must resolve into that worktree:

```text
<worktree>/chips/bk7258
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit
```

If they point at another checkout, stop and resolve the mapping before
building. In a shared workspace, changing symlinks is visible to other
processes. Prefer a serialized build, save both original link targets, and
restore them in a shell `trap` even when the build fails. Do not delete the
symlink targets or use a broad recursive cleanup.

The project manifest is the source of truth for the normal mapping. The build
tree consumes the mapped `vendor/` paths, while packaging scripts may be run
from the worktree because they locate the workspace by the `build.sh` and
`nuttx/` markers.

## 2. Configure and build CP/AP

Run from the parent workspace. Use the mapped path and keep the trailing slash:

```bash
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/ --cmake -j12
./build.sh vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/ap/ --cmake -j12
```

For a CP-only or Wi-Fi-disabled platform change, the first command is the
minimum build. Confirm the generated `.config` does not enable Wi-Fi/WPA when
the acceptance requires a normal CP configuration with Wi-Fi disabled.

`build.sh` derives output names from the board/config selection. Do not add a
random `-b` directory unless the task explicitly needs isolation:

```text
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/nuttx.elf
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/l1-validation.json
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/app1.bin
cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_ap/bk7258_ap/l1-validation.json
```

The normal build command supplies the project environment and compiler wrapper.
Direct `cmake --build` can fail with missing `ccache` or stale source paths and
is not equivalent evidence.

## 3. Package and independently decode

The default flow builds and packages the real CP plus OpenVela AP AMP image.
The bundled AP placeholder is recovery-only and must be selected explicitly
with `--placeholder`; it is expected to fail CPU1 AP release validation at
runtime.

For the repository-bundled recovery package, the project wrapper is the
preferred path:

```bash
<worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tools/bk7258-package.sh
```

It reads the CP/AP outputs, selects the real OpenVela AP profile, and runs the
independent decoder. The wrapper must print `decode       pass` before an image
is considered valid.

The default package slot intentionally replaces its previous package after the
new CP/AP build and L1 validation pass. `all-app.bin`, `manifest.json`, and
`decode-report.json` remain bound and are verified together before flashing.
Copy that trio elsewhere explicitly when a run must be preserved as historical
hardware evidence.

The package wrapper validates both L1 reports, invokes the container packer,
and independently decodes the final linear-CRC image. Do not flash `app.bin`
or `app1.bin` directly.

## 4. Offline regression checks

Run from the parent workspace or pass paths explicitly:

```bash
python3 <worktree>/board/bk7258-devkit/tests/test_bk7258_bundled_packaging.py
```

The decoder must produce the same report for relative and absolute input paths.
The report normalizes `image.path` with `Path.resolve()`; do not regress this
to the caller's spelling of the path, because evidence hashes and reports must
be stable across invocation directories.

For the vendor-input profile, first validate the machine-local input file and
then run the profile/package test described in
`board/bk7258-devkit/packaging/README.md`. Never invent vendor input paths or
copy credentials into the repository.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `No config file found at` | `build.sh` received `board/...` instead of mapped `vendor/...` path, or the path lacks the expected config directory | Run from the parent workspace with `vendor/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-devkit/configs/cp/` or `ap/` and verify `readlink -f` |
| Early `grep: dor/.../defconfig: No such file` followed by a valid `lunch`, build, and L1 pass | `build.sh` has a non-fatal path-slicing check before `lunch` for full mapped paths | Judge the final command result; do not treat this line alone as failure. A later `No config file found at` or nonzero build result is still a real failure |
| Output builds the wrong source checkout | Shared `vendor/` symlink points at another worktree | Save/replace the two BK7258 links for the build, serialize the operation, and restore them with a trap |
| Image size/config unexpectedly changes while build still passes | A standard CMake output directory retained another worktree's `.config` | Use `full_flow.sh`; its binding prevents cross-worktree cache reuse, and defconfig changes rebuild only the affected component slot |
| `ccache: not found` from direct CMake | Bypassed the environment setup used by `build.sh` | Re-run through `./build.sh ... --cmake` |
| CP image not found during packaging | CP build was not successful or used a custom output directory | Check `cmake_out/bk7258-devkit_cp/bk7258/app.bin`, its L1 report, and pass `--cp-app-bin` when using `-b` |
| Decoder report differs by working directory | Decoder received relative input and stored it verbatim | Use the current decoder that resolves `args.image`; run the path-stability regression |
| Too many generated directories | A one-shot workflow was used instead of the stable bound slot | Use the default `full_flow.sh`; it incrementally reuses one build slot and replaces one package slot per worktree |
| `Getting Bus...` keeps printing but `Gotten Bus...` never appears, then the manual-reset banner shows up | The automatic `reboot bootloader` did not engage: target firmware lacks the bootloader-reset patch, its console was hung, or the injection window was missed | Press reset on each numbered bell/banner from `notify_flash.py`; stop resetting after `Gotten Bus...`. Deploy `feature/bk7258-bootloader-reset` firmware for the automatic path |
| No reset prompt and no auto-reset banner are visible | Flash was launched without a PTY or through a buffered pipe | Run `full_flow.sh --flash` in an interactive terminal; do not redirect loader stdout |
| `GetBus fail` or `LinkCheck Timeout` | Reset timing, USB, downloader mode, or a busy serial port prevented handshake; Flash has not been erased yet | Close serial monitors and rerun the interactive flash stage |
| Flash refuses root or reports serial permission denied | Public workflow does not execute mutable worktree code as root | Add the user to the serial-device group, re-login, and run without `sudo` |
| Loader SHA-256 mismatch | The bundled proprietary loader differs from the audited repository version | Stop; review the binary change and update the pinned hash only through code review |

A successful host build proves compilation and L1 image validation only. A
passing package/decode proves the linear-CRC container contract. Hardware IRQ,
register readback, GPIO waveform, cold boot, and UART behavior require separate
target evidence and must not be claimed from this workflow alone.
